assumptions: DATA-DEC-01 and DATA-DEC-02 are Approved, which is what the data package says gates the DB-00 merge and the start of DB-00 coding.
A migration never applied to any database is reversible foundation under the G0 constraint.

acceptance_results.criterion: Every required_before_freeze item is assessed against the shipped schema and fixture list, not against a fixture count.
The assessment states plainly that it establishes PRESENCE of an artifact and not that the artifact satisfies the intent behind the phrase, with the specific items where that gap is widest named.
No contract status changes anywhere in the repository.
Contracts with a co-owner are routed to that co-owner rather than proposed for promotion by A0 alone.
npm run check stays green with no test skipped.

tests.result: see evidence/VERIFICATION.md, which is machine-written and compared byte-for-byte against a live run

security_privacy_cost_impact: data classification synthetic-only; secrets required false; network policy deny-unless-declared. No provider call, credential, migration or customer-data effect. Cost impact none: no metered resource is touched.
migration_and_data_impact: No migration is added or altered. The fixture's stored token digests are byte-identical before and after: measured 2026-09-06 that sha256(convert_to(t,'utf8')) equals digest(t,'sha256'), so no fixture identity moved.
compatibility_impact: None to any contract. Three repairs inside this package's own test harness and one to the CI shim, which now installs pgcrypto where the platform has it -- that last one makes CI STRICTER, and any code reaching for public.digest now fails there as it would on the instance.
known_limitations: The live half runs in CI and nowhere else. A Postgres service container gives db-migrate-clean, db-schema-lint and db-rls-smoke a real database on every pull request; all five migration batches apply and the schema lint passes. This DEVELOPMENT HOST still has no psql, pg_ctl or docker, so the targets refuse locally and every live change is proven by a CI round, not from a shell. db-migrate-upgrade and db-seed-replay remain unproven for a different reason: neither has a fixture to run against, and both say so rather than reporting a pass.

open_blockers[1] asked for the co-owner's signature on the role topology. A1 wrote its own record at evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/a1-countersignature-role-topology.md. READ THE VERDICT THERE: this manifest is written by A0 and does not speak for another role, so it does not restate it here.

What A0 can state, because it is a property of that document rather than a judgement about it: A1 re-measured the provisioned instance itself through ten read-only catalog queries rather than accepting A0's record, three of its findings contradict a record A0 wrote, and it declares in its own §0 that it is a subagent run in A0's vendor and model family assessing files it authored. It therefore does not satisfy independence.prefer_cross_vendor_review and does not lift the cross_vendor_exception this package already carries -- a second reading, not a second opinion.

The reservations that record raises are carried as the five blockers below, and they are open.

RESERVATION 1 (A1 §5.1). RFC-2026-016 §4 retired 'force RLS where compatible' and made an EXEMPTION REGISTER the control that replaces it. No such register exists anywhere in the repository. The phrase was retired for being unfalsifiable; its replacement is unfalsifiable by absence. Owner: A0, with RFC-2026-016's author.

RESERVATION 2 (A1 §5.2) — REPAIRED, and the repair is what is now asserted. scripts/db/run.mjs asserts no service role is SUPERUSER as well as no service role holds BYPASSRLS, refuses a snapshot whose service_roles carry no superuser field at all (an unmeasured property must not read as a passing one), and pins the instance's superuser set the way it already pinned the bypass set. Measured 2026-09-06 on xtvtflkntpqfvflvdbwk: all three service roles rolsuper false; supabase_admin is the only rolsuper on the instance.

RESERVATION 3 (A1 §5.3/§5.4). The record does not describe the tree in two places. 010_identity.sql:14 cites 'batch 004 corrects the record' and no 004_*.sql exists, so batch 000's pgcrypto claim is still wrong on both counts (pgcrypto is in `extensions`; gen_random_uuid is in pg_catalog). 000_foundation.sql:12 still calls an approved RFC 'Proposed'.

RESERVATION 4 (A1 §5.5) — REPAIRED at the call sites AND at the cause. The fixture and the invitation case now take the digest with pg_catalog's sha256(convert_to(...)), which resolves with no extension and no schema qualification; measured 2026-09-06 that it produces byte-identical output to extensions.digest(...,'sha256'), so no fixture identity moved. The cause was that the CI shim was MORE PERMISSIVE than the platform: batch 000's `create extension ... with schema public` is a no-op on the instance and succeeded in the container, so public.digest existed only in CI. The shim now installs pgcrypto in `extensions` where the platform has it, and the test that used to pin `public.digest(` now refuses any schema-qualified pgcrypto call.

RESERVATION 5 (A1 §5.6) — REPAIRED. expectDeniedBy holds a case to the layer it declares, and the runner applies it to every case carrying deniedBy. A policy refusal always names the policy; anything else saying permission denied is the privilege layer; anything that classifies as neither fails rather than guessing. Silence stays silence: a case declaring no layer is not checked.

Tenant isolation is proven against the CI container and measured once against a provisioned Supabase instance, and the two prove different things. In CI, 28 isolation cases pass on every run and a NEGATIVE CONTROL disables row level security on app.workspaces and requires the suite to fail -- it reports 10 of 28, so the suite is not blind. What CI cannot establish is the platform: its roles come from db/foundation/ci/supabase-shim.sql and were created by us, so a green run means the policies still do what they did, never that this holds on Supabase. The BYPASSRLS measurement behind DATA-DEC-03 came from the provisioned instance and has no CI equivalent. Batches 020 and above own the assertions SMOKE_COVERAGE names as uncovered.
Gate G0 remains Specification Baseline Complete / External Verification Pending.

recommended_next_work_packages: Provision a Postgres test instance and wire a runner, which turns six refusing targets into real checks.
Disposition of the policy-shape decision in WP-0A-A0-007, which unblocks the first tenant table.
DB-01 once batch 000 is merged and the live harness runs.
reviewer_instructions: The shim change is the one to read first. It makes CI match the platform on the one point where CI was more permissive, and that permissiveness is what let a fixture calling a function the instance does not have pass for weeks.
expectDeniedBy fails closed: an outcome that classifies as neither layer is refused rather than assumed to be the declared one. The test pins that, and pins that declaring no layer is not a claim.
Reservations 1 and 3 are NOT repaired here and remain open blockers.
